An object that's part of a data provider such as Oracle Provider for SQL Server.
The process of writing data to disk.
A structure in which elements are related to each other hierarchically.
A name, expression or string that resolves to a table.

A chain of attribute relationships that splits and rejoins but that contains no redundant relationships. For example, Day->Month->Year and Day->Quarter->Year have the same start and end points, but do not have any common relationships.
A feature that tracks and stores a record of a shared document when it is first created, and each time it is edited.
A set of logical pre-defined properties that model the behavior or characteristics for certain types of managed targets (such as a database, table, login, view,etc) in policy-based management.
A component of SQL Server 2005 Integration Services that manipulates data.
Conditions that users specify to limit which records are included in the result set of a query.

An Exchange Server 2007 connector that uses a Drop directory on a Hub Transport server to send messages to a local messaging server that doesn't use the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) as its primary transport mechanism.

An import of all data from a file, or a scoped view, of a connected data source to the connector space. Data from the connected data source is compared with data in the connector space. If there are no attribute changes, the object is not changed in the connector space.
In the Exchange Server user interface, the main tab on the properties page.

In Exchange Server 2007, a journal rule that processes all email messages that pass through a Hub Transport server. This includes email messages that were already processed by the external and internal rules.

In Exchange Server 2007, the feature that the Exchange administrator configures to enable functionality provided by IP Allow List Provider services that compile lists of IP addresses that are known not to have sent spam in the past. The Connection Filter agent queries the service to determine if a given IP address is "safe."
Configuration that is used by the Connection Filter agent to query an IP Allow List provider.
A business that compiles and distributes lists of IP addresses that are known not to have sent spam in the past.

In Exchange Server 2007, the feature that the Exchange administrator configures to enable functionality provided by IP Block List Provider services that compile lists of IP addresses from which spam has originated in the past.

An email message that is automatically sent by Microsoft Exchange to the owners of a mailbox or a public folder when a size limit, which is called a storage quota, for the mailbox or public folder has been exceeded or is at risk of being exceeded.
An administrator-defined list of recipients for which mail coming in from the Internet should never be accepted.

An advanced speech codec that is designed for real-time two-way Voice over IP (VoIP) applications such as gaming, audio conferencing, and wireless applications over IP. RTAudio is the preferred Microsoft audio codec and is the default codec for Microsoft Unified Communications platforms.

A project containing one or more inserted projects. These can retain links to their source projects and may be linked to one another.

The amount of work that has been performed on a task or assignment.

A constraint that applies to two elements, such as two classes or two associations. The constraint is shown as a dashed arrow from one element to the other, labeled by the constraint string in braces ({ }).
In an activity diagram, a type of state that has an internal action and at least one outgoing transition that involves the explicit events of completing the internal action.
The page that is currently available for editing in a document.
A special case of a statechart diagram in which all of the states are action states and the transitions are triggered by the completion of actions in the source state.
A schedule for planning the activities that often follow the completion of a project.

The basic component of a ROOM structure diagram. The space inside the actor can contain actor references, behavior end ports, reference ports, bindings, and layer connections. The border can contain class relay ports and class end ports.
The actors that define components of your structure diagram. Actor references can appear only inside an actor class. An actor reference can have reference ports on its outside border.

A Microsoft Access project (.adp) file with all modules compiled and all editable source code removed.
The process of documenting and archiving a project in a timely manner, as well as formally accepting the project's product and lessons learned.
The rectangle that appears around shapes and objects from other applications as you move them.

The angle of the orientation of a shape's local coordinate system with respect to its parent coordinate system. The angle of rotation is specified in the Angle cell of the Shape Transform section in a ShapeSheet spreadsheet.

An enterprise resource who is responsible for entering progress information in Project Web Access. This person can be different than the person initially assigned to the task.

A view that shows the resources assigned to each task as well as the total and time-phased work and cost information for each assignment. The two assignment views are the Task Usage and Resource Usage views.
The end of a binary or other association where it connects to a class. By associating properties with an association end, you can indicate the role or direction.

A type of collaboration role that describes the relationship between two ClassifierRoles. It is represented by a path between two class role elements and can include the underlined name of the corresponding association.
In a static structure diagram, a use of a parameterized class, or template, in which the parameters from the parameterized class are bound to actual values.
The distance from the midpoint of a circular arc to the midpoint of the arc's chord.

A menu that is available by default in an application; it is not created by the user.
The formatting attributes that are available by default in an application's style list.
A Project view that displays a project's tasks in a calendar format.

Code that enforces constraints on a table or column.

A constraint that allows for business rules that span multiple tables. For example, the Order table could have a CHECK constraint that would prevent orders for a customer from exceeding a credit limit defined for the customer in the Customer table.
A control that is used to present a set of mutually exclusive choices. By default, a choice group contains two choice sections, one of which appears to the user as the default choice in the form.
The point at which transitions split into multiple, mutually exclusive branches, each terminating at a different destination state. One of the branches must be a default branch.
A small overlap that decreases the knockout of the lower of two differently colored, abutting objects.
A superclass that includes class, data type, and interface subclasses. Because all classifier subclasses share the same syntax, they are all represented by the same rectangle model element.
A type of collaboration role that is a slot for an object in a collaboration. It is represented by the class rectangle symbol with only the name compartment showing.

The format that you define for a work breakdown structure [WBS] code or a custom outline code. The mask specifies the sequence and number of letters or numbers required for each level and the symbol separating the levels.
In Visual Basic for Applications, the window that is used to display, edit, and write module-level and procedure code.

A collection of modeling elements that interact within a given context to perform an operation or a use case. The objects in a collaboration are roles describing types of objects rather than representations of the objects themselves.
An interaction diagram that shows, for one system event described by one use case, how a group of objects collaborate with one another.

A keyword or phrase with an associated color that helps you keep track of items, such as messages, contacts, and appointments. You can use color categories to easily find, sort, filter, or group items.
The part of PivotTable view that contains column fields.
A supplemental program with the filename extension .dll or .exe that extends the capabilities of a program by adding custom commands and specialized features.

A resource that is formally allocated to any task assignments they have within a project.

An implementation diagram that shows the structure of the code itself.
A high-level object made of tightly bound parts. A composite object is an instance of a composite class, which implies the composition aggregation between the class and its parts.
In a statechart diagram, a state that has been decomposed into concurrent (representing and relationships) or mutually exclusive (representing or relationships) substates.
A format, such as cell shading or font color, that Excel automatically applies to cells if a specified condition is true.
The type of Web Part connection. For example, the Provide Row To connection type passes a row of data from one Web Part to another Web Part.
A view of an individual contact that contains all the information stored in the contact.

A collection of information about a resource's rates, including the standard rate, overtime rate, any per-use cost, and the date when the pay rate takes effect. You can establish up to five different cost rate tables for each resource.
A resource that doesn't depend on the amount of work on a task or the duration of a task, such as airfare or lodging.

A task that must be completed on schedule for the project to finish on time. If a critical task is delayed, the project completion date might also be delayed. A series of critical tasks makes up a project's critical path.

Printed information about tasks and resources over a specified time period. There are five predefined crosstab reports in Project: Cash Flow, Crosstab, Resource Usage, Task Usage, and Who Does What When.
A specification language for describing data structures. You can use the Crow's Foot entity and relationship shapes to diagram the structure of databases.

A color in the Visio application that is stored with a shape as an RGB or HSL value rather than as an index to the document's color palette. A custom color is saved only with the shape to which it is applied.

The amount of time between the scheduled start of a task and the time when work should actually begin on the task.

A Visio file (template) with a .vst extension that opens with the stencils, styles, and settings you need to create a particular type of drawing.

A type of field whose content is expressed as a duration of time. Examples include the Work, Duration, and Delay fields. A duration field includes the duration unit, such as hour, day, or week.
A standard format used by CAD programs (such as Autodesk AutoCAD) to store drawing files.
The earliest date that a task could possibly be completed, based on early finish dates of predecessor and successor tasks, other constraints, and any leveling delay.

The process of Access updating or repainting the screen while a macro is running.

The default method of scheduling in Project; the duration of a task shortens or lengthens as resources are added or removed from a task, while the amount of effort necessary to complete a task remains unchanged.
