The price provided by the manufacturer as the retail price of products licensed or sold through a distribution channel. This is recommended only - actual prices are determined between the customer and the direct seller.

The price provided by the manufacturer as the retail price of products licensed or sold through a distribution channel. This is recommended only - actual prices are determined between the customer and the direct seller.
A warranty that the parties to a contract expressly agree to either in writing or orally.
An amount paid for products, advice or services.
To repair an error in coding or logic that caused a program to malfunction or to produce incorrect results, or to modify or enhance a product, or its derivatives.
Relief for any foreign taxes paid on taxable income or profit.
When referring to a Microsoft licensing program, any product Microsoft makes available for license without charge.
An operating system license that relates to the complete version of the operating system and not an upgrade or an update.
Something that operates in effectively the same way and serves the same purpose.
The legislative statement of all the private, non-commercial law in effect in Germany.
The legislative statement of all the commercial law in effect in Germany.
The Product Liability Act in effect in Germany.
When appearing in the name or header of a Microsoft Volume Licensing Agreement, an indication that the agreement is applicable to a government entity.
A Microsoft volume licensing contract available for small and mid-sized government entities that provides a license grant on a subscription basis.
A Microsoft volume licensing contract available for small and mid-sized government entities that provides a license grant on a perpetual basis.
To provide or permit access to.
A great degree of negligence that is willful and conscious.
A value-added tax levied in some countries/regions.
A value-added tax levied in some countries/regions.
To give an assurance that an agreement or any other legal act will be executed.
To undertake to be liable for the debt or default of another.
A promise that an agreement or any other legal act will be executed.
The legislative statement of all the private, non-commercial law in effect in Hungary.
Pertaining to something prohibited by law.
A warranty that is not explicitly agreed to by the parties but is automatically imposed by the operation of law, i.e. by a statute or by a court to implement the intent of the parties.
In an honest and truthful way.
The set of standard trade definitions used in international sales contracts devised and published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
An individual or entity that does not have an employment contract (and is not an employee), but rather has a contract for service where he/she/it is entrusted to carry out a specific project.

When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, an enrollment that is entered into between Microsoft and the Customer but where the licenses are paid for through a distribution channel involving a reseller which purchases and resells the licenses.
When referring to intellectual property, to violate an intellectual property right (such as copyright, trademark or patent).
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, the length of time a new agreement or enrollment stays in effect before its renewal or replacement by a new agreement (often for three years).
A remedy in the form of a court order that either requires or forbids a certain action to be carried out (or forbids the continuation of an action).
When referring to a Microsoft licensing agreement, an inspection carried out by a customer of its own compliance with the requirements of the license agreement.
An international organization that works to promote global trade and investment.
A compilation of knowledge that can be shared, modified, revised and manipulated.
The language selected and favored by a customer.
A fee charged for the delayed payment of an amount due.
The underlying legal arguments and support for a claim.
When referring to interest rates, the maximum rate of interest imposed by law that may be charged.
The beneficiary of a license grant.
When referring to a Microsoft license agreement, the documentation that constitutes evidence of a customer's license grant.
The person or entity that grants a license.
A manufacturer's estimated retail price for a product as it appears on its published price list.
When referring to a Microsoft license agreement, the place in which a person or entity is located.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, the form used by volume licensing customers to select the software media to be delivered to it pursuant to its agreement or enrollment.
The products traded.
A legal entity that is an affiliate of a Microsoft entity.

desc: A letter confirming Microsoft's approval to extend credit to a volume licensing customer through the Microsoft Financing program.
A legacy Microsoft volume licensing agreement that preceded the Open Value Program.
A legacy Microsoft volume licensing agreement that preceded the Select Agreement.
The license management Web site for Microsoft volume licensing customers that displays a customer's license status, agreement numbers, online records, and other license information.
The license management Web site for Microsoft volume licensing customers that displays a customer's license status, agreement numbers, online records, and other license information.
The unlawful use of something lawfully held.

When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, a form that may be incorporated into an enrollment or agreement that lists previous enrollments and/or agreements being renewed or consolidated into the new enrollment/agreement.
When referring to the disclosure of information, a principle to disclose the information only to those directly concerned and impacted by it.
A place on a computer network where a file originates or is located.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, an option available to license products on only a selection of desktops in the customer's company.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, a service provided over the Internet that volume licensing customers may subscribe to.
The practice of making the source code (program instructions) for a software product freely available, at no cost, to third parties.
The documentation evidencing a customer's order.

When referring to Microsoft licensing programs, a vendor engaged by a customer to either lease-finance its acquisitions under the enrollment or to manage information and data systems assets that include software licenses on behalf of the customer.
An agreement that includes outsourcer terms and conditions.
An agreement that includes outsourcer terms and conditions.
The terms and conditions applicable to the outsourcer and the outsourcing arrangement.
A part of an entity.
An amount of money that is payable and overdue.
The grant of a right by a government to exclude the making, using or selling of an invention by any other person for a period of time.
One of the ways available to make payment.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, a discount applied if the customer opts to license a desktop platform under its agreement with Microsoft.
A place where individuals and goods are examined and cleared by customs officials in order to lawfully enter a country/region.
The prices for a product, license or service.
A list of products available under Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs. The product list sets out which products are available under each program and any additional applicable terms and conditions.
A document that specifies the terms and conditions applicable to the use of products licensed under Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs.
When referring to a Microsoft Enterprise or Enterprise Subscription Agreement, a type of desktop platform comprised of Windows Upgrade, Office Professional and Core CAL.
Pertaining to information or property (including products) belonging to or controlled by a person or entity.
A sales tax applied in Canada by each Province.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, an existing prior enrollment that meets the applicable criteria in order to qualify for certain rights under the applicable license agreement.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, a government organization that meets the criteria required to participate under Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs as a government customer.

When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, the form submitted by a qualifying government entity confirming that it meets the criteria required to participate under Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs as a government customer.

When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, an operating system that the customer must run on its desktops in order to be eligible to license the upgrade version available under the volume licensing programs. The list of qualifying operating systems is set out in the product list.

When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, an operating system license that the customer must have in order to be eligible to acquire the upgrade license available under the volume licensing programs. The list of qualifying operating systems is set out in the product list.
The estimated retail prices of licenses sold through a reseller or distribution channel.
The means to impose, safeguard or recover a right or to obtain redress for an infringement of a right.
When referring to money, to send a sum of money as payment for something.
To make a statement of fact or promise (often used to induce someone to enter into an agreement).
To sell a product or service which you bought.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, a unique number allocated to the reseller by the relevant regional operations center.

A Microsoft volume licensing contract available for large companies and government organizations that provides a license grant on a perpetual basis and where the customer forecasts its purchases over that term of the agreement.
An enrollment entered into by a Select customer - either an entity that has entered into a Select Agreement or one of its affiliates.

A Microsoft volume licensing program available to large companies and government organizations that provides a license grant on a perpetual basis and where the customer forecasts its purchases over that term of the Select Agreement.

An enrollment entered into by a Select customer and a vendor engaged by the Select customer to lease-finance its acquisitions under the enrollment, or to manage information and data systems assets that include software licenses on behalf of the Select customer.
A form completed by a Select Agreement customer indicating its forecasted purchase of licenses under the Select program during the term of the Select Agreement.
When referring to Microsoft licensing and partner programs, the template questionnaire provided by Microsoft that the customer or partner would complete when conducting an internal audit.
A form of risk management where an enterprise or organization establishes a reserve to protect itself from future loss rather than purchasing insurance.

When referring to the clause of a contract, a provision that maintains the rest of the contract in effect if any other provision is held to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable. If possible the contract will avoid total invalidity by severing the illegal, invalid or unenforceable provisions so that the rest of the contract will remain in effect.
The act of sending goods or a group of goods shipped.
A single license available for sale in retail shops.
The Commercial Code in effect in Slovakia.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, the extent of Software Assurance rights and benefits that cover licenses included under a volume licensing agreement.
A tax collected on the issue or transfer of securities. It was originally a tax collected by stamping the instruments that gave effect to a transaction.
The body of law derived from Acts passed by a legislative authority.
Liability based on the breach of an absolute obligation to meet a certain standard or make something safe, where negligence or fault does not need to be proved.
An individual or organization that carries out work on behalf of another company or person.
A license granted by a licensee or sublicensee covering some or all of the rights granted to it under the initial license acquired by it.
To take the place of.

When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, contact details provided by the customer of additional persons in its organization that shall receive information and notices under the agreement, in addition to the contacts already listed in the agreement.
When referring to Microsoft Volume Licensing Programs, the form that a customer completes to provide Supplemental Contact Information.
A tax or duty imposed by a government on certain types of goods when they are imported into a country/region, and sometimes on goods exported.
A monetary amount that may be set against an entity or individual's tax liability.
Pertaining to products, activities and employee or corporate income that are not subject to tax.
A geographic area.
An Australian Act relating to the conduct of trade.
A court or any other body set up to settle disputes.
When referring to software, a full copy of a software product.

When referring to the Microsoft Enterprise program, an annual count of the number of qualified desktops, users, and additional products that have been added to the customer's organization during the year and for which licenses must be ordered going forward.
When referring to the Microsoft Enterprise program, the annual order placed by the customer to cover the qualified desktops, users and additional products included in its true-up count.
When referring to the Microsoft Enterprise program, the price or reference price applicable to the annual true-up orders.
Not connected as an affiliate.
The arbitration rules of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law.

arabic: ترخيص نظام تشغيل سطح المكتب الأساسي
desc: The full operating system license that gives the right to and must be purchased at the same time as or prior to an operating system upgrade license.
The full license that gives the right to and must be purchased at the same time as or prior to an upgrade license.
When referring to a contract, pertaining to an agreement or clause that, even if it is valid, cannot be enforced.
A model statute in the United States (enacted by most states) which sets out the definition of what constitutes a trade secret.
The act of using a product that does not conform with or is not permitted by the law.

When referring to the Microsoft Enterprise volume licensing program, a form submitted by the customer to Microsoft to confirm there is no change to the number of Qualified Desktops, Qualified Users, and/or Additional Products run since the last anniversary of its enrollment.
A legacy Microsoft volume licensing offering giving the right to upgrade a product licensed under the agreement/enrollment.
The amount and extent of upgrade rights that cover licenses included under a volume licensing agreement.
The information provided with a product by a manufacturer describing how to use a product.
The information provided with a product by a manufacturer describing how to use a product.
The information provided with a product by a manufacturer describing how to use a product.
Having no legal effect.
The relinquishment or abandonment of a legal right, or the abstention from asserting it.

english: implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose
desc: When referring to a product sold or licensed and when the seller or licensor knows the buyer is purchasing a product or license for a particular purpose, a warranty implied by law that a product is suitable for that purpose.

When referring to a product sold or licensed, a warranty implied by law that the product meets the standard of quality that would be reasonably expected by a consumers and persons in that trade i.e. that it is fit for the ordinary purpose for which such goods are used.
When referring to a product sold or licensed, a warranty that the product does not violate any intellectual property right.
When referring to a product sold or licensed, a warranty implied by law that the product will meet a standard that any reasonable person would consider as satisfactory.
When referring to a product sold or licensed, a warranty that the seller or licensor has title to the product.
A service provided via the World Wide Web.
When referring to taxation, to deduct funds from salary or other income to cover tax liability.
A notice provided in written format (sometimes includes email format).
The extent of financial protection provided by an insurance policy/program.
A set of data items that contains a unique identifier, called a key, and a value that is the actual data for the key.

Pertaining to the combination of a 64-bit Windows operating system and microprocessors that natively support the x86 for extended systems (x64) 64-bit instruction set. Examples include AMD Opteron and Intel Xeon with 64-bit extension technology processors.

Pertaining to the combination of a 32-bit Windows operating system and a microprocessor that natively supports the 32-bit x86 instruction set. Examples include Intel Pentium 4, AMD Athlon and VIA C7 processors.

A situation that occurs when a Web page loaded in one URL security zone loads a page from a less restrictive zone in a frame or a new window. For example, if a page from the Internet zone loads a page from the Local Machine zone, a zone elevation has occurred.
A component attached to HTML elements which encapsulate specific functionality.

A small piece of code that intercepts API calls from applications, transforming them so that Windows Vista will provide the same product support for the application as previous versions of the operating system.
An account in the Administrators group of Windows Vista. Users with this account type must consent to perform administrative activities.
To tap a device screen and hold one's finger or stylus in place.
A program that extends the capabilities of a browser.
A system that allows users to send and receive messages when they are out of range.
A list of things to be done or considered.

A software accessory that enables you to use a variety of direct input methods (such as handwriting, speech, touch, stylus, gestures, and so on) to interact with Windows-based programs. An input panel can include a writing pad and a character pad to convert handwriting into typed text or mathematical equations, and an on-screen keyboard to enter individual characters.
A card, inserted into a portable device, used to store files.
A computer service that issues digital certificates that can only be used inside a business or organization.
An area in Windows Photo Gallery that includes an assortment of picture editing tools for common editing tasks. The Fix pane is opened by clicking the Fix button on the toolbar in Photo Gallery.
A file storage system that can be used to create CDs and DVDs. Discs formatted with Live File System allow you to copy files to the disc at any time, instead of copying (burning) them all at once.

A file system used to create CDs and DVDs. Discs created using the Mastered format are more likely to be compatible with older computers, but an additional step is required to burn the collection of files to the disc.
A removable storage device, such as an external hard disk or USB flash drive, used for increasing storage space on a computer or for transferring information between computers.

A list of files that match specific search or filter information. You can save a search created in the Search folder. Whenever you open a saved search, it will search your computer again to find all files that match what you're looking for.
Information about your specific speaking style and environment that helps Speech Recognition to better understand the commands you say.

An instruction that tells Windows Firewall to open a port briefly, allow a program or service to pass a specific piece of information through, and then close the port. These instructions are called "exceptions" because normally the firewall blocks all unsolicited attempts to send information.
The name used to identify a wireless network.
Information about a wireless network, such as the wireless network name, service set identifier (SSID), network adapter used to connect to the network, default icon, and default printer.

A folder containing your most frequently used folders (such as Documents, Pictures, Music, Favorites, Contacts, and other folders that are specific to your user account). The personal folder is labeled with the name you use to log on to your computer and is located at the top of the Start menu.

The folder in Windows where you store files that you want to share with other people on the same computer or network. The Public folder is located in the Users folder of your root directory (for example, C:\Users\Public).

A collection of visual elements and sounds for your computer desktop or device User Interface. A theme determines the look of the various visual elements of your User Interface, such as windows, icons, fonts, and colors, and it can include sounds.

The Internet Explorer feature that allows users to surf the Web without leaving a browsing history, cookies or other information on the PC so they can do online banking on a shared computer, for example.
An application that formats and displays trace messages.
To recompile the source versions in order to produce a named set of deliverables (software components).
The use of Visual Studio on one computer (the host computer) to debug an application that is running on another computer (the target or remote computer).
An expression or a variable that appears in the Watch window.
A Visual Studio debugging window that is available in break mode and that provides the value of a variable or an expression.
The service for wireless products that allows users to send and receive brief messages consisting of text and numbers to and from mobile phones and devices.
A software component that manages the distribution of memory resources in SQL Server.
To protect a project from being affected by certain commands, for example, Check Out, Check In, and Undo Check Out.
A computer that is part of a OneCare circle but is not a hub PC or a monitor PC. A device PC has no privileges to monitor or make changes to any other computer in the OneCare circle.
An Internet Explorer security feature that stops scripts and Document Object Model (DOM) objects from executing across domains.
A configured Windows image that includes additional software applications and updated drivers. A single reference installation image can be deployed onto many destination computers.
The collection of recurring job definitions and schedules associated with a protection group.
A card that connects to an expansion bus and contains one or more devices.
A single Windows image in a Windows image (.wim) file.

A computer that is not the hub PC but that monitors the activity of other computers in the OneCare circle. The OneCare subscription administrator designates which, if any, computers in the circle have monitoring privileges. A monitor PC cannot make changes to any other computer in the OneCare circle.
A set of statistics that shows the results of a single run of a management agent.

A virtual community that provides people with opportunities to interact (via blogs, chats, newsgroups, webcasts, user groups, and forums) with Microsoft employees, experts, and peers in order to share knowledge and news about Microsoft technology.

A unique identifier made from three otherwise separate pieces of information. For example, a color can be specified by a red, blue, green triplet. Triplets are the second most common type of ID after single, or unique, IDs.
An application that enables tracing and connects the trace provider with the trace consumer.
A voice command that can be executed by the user at any time and performs an action that typically saves a lot of clicks.
The sound made by a mobile device or other phone to indicate an incoming call or message, for example, a series of beeps or an audio recording.

An editor that enables users to create ringtones from sound files on their PC or create custom recordings. It also enables them to preview and save them directly to their phone as the primary ringtone, or assign them to one or more contacts.
A calendar view that displays all scheduled items.
An alert that is set by the user to be activated at a particular time.
An extension to SQM that allows Microsoft to cause clients sending reports matching a pattern to perform some predefined action.
A wizard that enables users to either import licenses from one license server on to another or re-install licenses previously installed in their server by re-building the license server database.
The original Windows operating system image file or the OEM custom Windows operating system image.

An authentication device that digitally scans an individual's fingerprint, records the unique pattern of the individual's ridges and valleys, and determines if the pattern matches the pattern of the person who has access permission to a particular device, such as a computer or a phone, or to a Web site.
A renamed .cab file which contains a .theme file, and optionally one or more desktop backgrounds, icons, mouse pointer files, and sound files. It does not contain executables or screen savers.
A renamed .cab file which contains a .theme file, and optionally one or more desktop backgrounds, icons, mouse pointer files, and sound files. It does not contain executables or screen savers.
A renamed .ini file that points to the theme resources and contains theme values such as colors, fonts, and window size metrics.
A file of supported type used in a theme.
A server that sends out data to a spoke server.
A certificate that identifies the certification authority (CA) that issues server and client authentication certificates to the servers and clients that request these certificates.

A release process used internally at Microsoft to track the extra processes, such as additional testing, required to post a hotfix on Microsoft public Web sites or to allow a third party the ability to distribute a hotfix, such as an OEM pre-installing a hotfix prior to shipping to a customer.
A product that is generally available to the marketplace or a section of the marketplace and which is available for license for a fee.
The government entity that imposes a tax.
The privilege of an administrator of a computer system to control which users have the right to perform various administrative functions.
A folder that stores the user's graphics, e.g. digital pictures. Many graphic design and photo-editing programs use this location by default to open or save graphic files.
A button that replaces the File menu beginning with some 2007 Microsoft Office system programs.
A button that replaces the File menu beginning with some 2007 Microsoft Office system programs.
A keyboard shortcut that is displayed over the option to which it corresponds in the user interface and tells the user which key(s) can be used to access or activate that feature or command.
A series of digital-media files that users can subscribe to online, that are sent to their computers or mobile devices and that can then be accessed on demand on the users' reader.
A type of security threat in which a malicious user is able to derive the value of data without actually accessing it, for example by monitoring the response time to a query.
The specified area around a control that activates the display of a tooltip when the mouse pauses on it.
One of the primary colors of ink in the CMYK color model used in printing, whose name is derived from the dye magenta. A color from the Outlook calendar color palette.

A service that improves information workers' free/busy data by providing secure, consistent, and up-to-date free/busy information to computers that are running Microsoft Office Outlook 2007. By default, this service is installed with Exchange 2007.

A mechanism that is used to deliver messages at an interim hop, along the least-cost routing path. A backoff occur when direct relay fails for any reason, such as network issues or servers going offline. The routing component tries to deliver messages as close to the destination as possible by backing off, hop by hop, along the least-cost routing path until a connection is made.
One of four Exchange 2007 administrator roles. Members of this role have full access to all Exchange properties and objects in the Exchange organization.

One of four Exchange 2007 administrator roles. Members of this role have permissions to modify any Exchange property on an Active Directory user, contact, group, dynamic distribution group, or public folder object.

One of four Exchange 2007 administrator roles. Members of this role have access to only local server Exchange configuration data, either in Active Directory or on the physical computer on which Active Directory is installed.

arabic: دور مسؤولو العرض فقط في Exchange
desc: One of four Exchange 2007 administrator roles. Members of this role have read-only access to the entire Exchange organization tree in the Active Directory configuration container, and read-only access to all Windows domain containers that have Exchange recipients.

A method that defines a low-level API to the underlying database structures in Exchange Server. Extensible Storage Engine is also used by other databases, such as the Active Directory directory service database.

A mailbox that represents conference rooms and company equipment. Resource mailboxes can be included as resources in meeting requests, providing a simple and efficient way to utilize resources for an organization. The user account that is associated with a resource mailbox is disabled.

A replication that uses the same log shipping and replay technology used by local continuous replication (LCR) and cluster continuous replication (CCR) to provide added deployment options and configurations.
To monitor an email conversation or newsgroup thread. The headers for messages in a watched conversation appear in a different color, which makes them easier to find in a message list.
A Wizard-based interface for maximizing battery life based on user preferences.

An option on the Views menu in File Explorer that shows the most appropriate details for the file type in a flexible layout rather than only showing the details associated with the column headers in the view.
A data packet that is typically sent to create or maintain a NAT mapping and consists of an IPv6 header with no IPv6 payload.
A Microsoft proprietary compression algorithm highly tuned for speed. It achieves ZIP-level compression ratios and is currently the server-side compression implementation of choice within Microsoft.

A Win32 service process that optimizes performance of applications by caching commonly used font data. Applications will start this service if it is not already running. It can be disabled, though doing so will degrade application performance.

arabic: خدمة الذاكرة المؤقتة للخطوط في Windows
desc: A Win32 service process that optimizes performance of applications by caching commonly used font data. Applications will start this service if it is not already running. It can be disabled, though doing so will degrade application performance.
The feature in Control Panel that provides the user with a single point of entry for tasks and notifications related to security and general PC software maintenance.
A Microsoft SQL Server tool designed to limit the performance of an instance of the database engine any time more than eight operations are active at the same time.
To remove the cloaked attribute from a project.
To remove the cloaked attribute from a project.

A gallery that allows users to create a quick rule to move mail to a selected folder based on the sender, recipients, or conversation of the currently selected email message without opening the full Create Rule dialog.
A group of computers on a home network that can share pictures, music, videos, documents, and printers. A homegroup is created by using the HomeGroup feature; it is protected with a password.
A password that helps prevent unauthorized access to homegroup files and printers.
A digital or paper format pack that usually consists of a proof of purchase, the description of the licensing terms and policies, and number of client access licenses (CALs) purchased in this pack.
An action that removes redundant messages from an email conversation to reduce information overload and improve readability.
To confer with the call recipient before transferring a call or adding the call recipient to a conference call.
A note you type on the Notes tab of a conversation window to potentially be forwarded along with the call and saved in the call history.
An instant message session with multiple parties, exchanged via IM (not through your mobile operator).
An instant message session with multiple parties, exchanged via IM (not through your mobile operator).
An instant message session with multiple parties, exchanged via IM (not through your mobile operator).
A flag that can be set for Lync and Communicator calls or instant messages to indicate the urgency of the conversation.
A proprietary phone connected to a PBX.
A menu item that opens an Outlook meeting invitation prepopulated with the selected contact(s).

A method of building computer systems in which the system is programmed and implemented in segments, rather than waiting until the entire project is completed for implementation. Developed by programmer James Martin, RAD uses such tools as CASE and visual programming.

A method of building computer systems in which the system is programmed and implemented in segments, rather than waiting until the entire project is completed for implementation. Developed by programmer James Martin, RAD uses such tools as CASE and visual programming.
In synchronization processes, the current knowledge of the source replica, to be used in conflict detection.
A feature that replicates formatting from a source item — such as text in Word, a cell in Excel, a control in Access, or a shape in Publisher — to one or more target items.

A wizard that is used by advanced users to perform specific operations on their existing virtual hard disks such as compacting their virtual hard disk, merging it, converting it to another type or expanding its size.
A series of digital media files (audio or video) delivered to users over the Web.

A wizard that is used by advanced users to create custom virtual hard disks for virtual machines. The purpose of the New Virtual Hard Disk Wizard is to gather the basic information from the user necessary to create a new virtual hard disk.

An account attribution that allows users to use the computer in the exploratory mode which will automatically discard changes and actions upon logoff. Guest Mode can be applied to the standard user account in Windows 7 enabling PC owners to safely share the computer with guests, children, or other family member, with a peace of mind knowing no damaging changes or unauthorized disk writes will be made to their computer.
A collection of items, such as files and folders, assembled from various locations. The locations might be on your computer, an external hard drive, removable media, or someone else’s computer.
A collection of items, such as files and folders, assembled from various locations. The locations might be on your computer, an external hard drive, removable media, or someone else’s computer.
To mark an item so that it always appears in a specific place in the UI or in a list.
To remove an item, such as a tile, library, movie, game, or app, from a given area of the UI, to make it inaccessible in that area.
A Windows accessory that enables handwritten input of math expressions as well as easy-to-use correction of recognition results. Its functionality is analogous to that of Tablet Input Panel.
An expression that uses numeric values, such as integers, fixed-point numbers, and floating-point numbers, and operators, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
A user with role-based permission who can change settings for apps, services, users, subscriptions, and/or devices.
The computers that share a OneCare subscription.

A device that receives an action specified by the OneCare administrator. For example, an external hard drive that is the designated the place for file backup would be considered to be the "target device" of the backup function.
A person with whom a Windows Live user has established a mutual social connection.
To come upon through action.
To come upon through action.

Someone who has been specified by a manager (or other person) to make or receive calls on their behalf. Delegates can change call forwarding settings and add other delegates. Delegates are automatically given “Team Access,” which allows them to contact the “manager” even when his or her presence is set to Do not Disturb.

arabic: مكون التحكم في إدخال العمليات الرياضية
desc: A control that provides integration of math handwriting recognition functionality into other applications. This control is for applications that want to include math recognition functionality but do not want to fully implement their own math recognition user interface.
The process of using a “machine” (in most cases computer software) to translate text from one human language to another.
The ActiveX control of the Math Input Panel and Math Input Control that handles inking, recognizer calls, and correction experience.
The ActiveX control of the Math Input Panel and Math Input Control in charge of displaying handwriting recognition result in real time, the recognizer state, error messages and hints.
A pencil tool that works with texture and simulates a real life pencil in stroke.

arabic: النظام الأساسي لأداة الاستشعار والموقع في Windows
desc: A Windows platform that provides a standard way for device manufacturers to expose sensor devices to software developers and consumers, while providing developers with a standardized application programming interface (API) for working with sensors and sensor data. Examples of sensors include ambient light sensors, location sensors, motion detection sensors, etc.
A Windows feature that enables users to easily roll back their PC to an earlier good state while keeping their data safe.

A privileged Windows service that interfaces with biometric hardware through the Windows Biometric Driver Interface, and manages the capture, matching and storage of biometric data, and exposes this capability to applications through the Windows Biometric API.
A button that allows you to quickly toggle between Player Mode and Library Mode in Windows Media Player.
A list of incoming calls and outgoing calls, showing information such as the name of the caller or call recipient, the date and the time of the call.

arabic: الوظيفة الإضافية لإجراء المؤتمرات من خلال Microsoft Outlook
desc: A Microsoft Outlook add-in that allows you to schedule a Live Meeting or Lync or Office Communicator conference call from Outlook.
Dial in to the audio conferencing provider from your physical telephone when the audio conferencing provider service cannot call you.
Pertaining to a connection that has ended.
A contact within a group in the Contacts list.
A video stream from a source that is external to the user's computer.
The large video feed in a conversation window.

A component that consists of properties, rules, and rules extensions that determine how an object is processed in the metadirectory. A single management agent can have one or more run profiles that determine the management agent's behavior, such as how or when the management agent runs.
The Profiler Performance Report view that helps to automate the process of locating a performance bottleneck.

In a call queue, a method of sending calls to agents whereby incoming calls ring all call agents one by one, from the beginning of the call agent list. If an agent dismisses or does not pick up a call, the call will ring the next agent and will try all agents until it is picked up or times out.
A rule that is executed by the SharePoint Maintenance Manager to identify problems that are related to configuration settings, data integrity, performance, security, and other issues.
An administrative tool that examines a computer, server farm, or server cluster against an optimal set of procedures and functional principles for that configuration, and reports possible issues.
An open source scripting language that can be embedded in HTML documents to execute interactive functions on a Web server. It is generally used for Web development.
An open source scripting language that can be embedded in HTML documents to execute interactive functions on a Web server. It is generally used for Web development.
A process by which multiple authors edit a shared document simultaneously, or collaborate effectively even when they are not online at the same time.

A type of Groove workspace that is an offline, personal copy of a SharePoint site and is kept in sync with the corresponding SharePoint site providing a convenient way of working with SharePoint content, even when the SharePoint site is not available.

A client-side cache for documents that are stored on Web servers. Documents are seamlessly replicated from this local cache, and uploaded to servers as required, enabling faster and more robust file access.

A client-side cache for documents that are stored on Web servers. Documents are seamlessly replicated from this local cache, and uploaded to servers as required, enabling faster and more robust file access.
A feature that breaks a file up into granular chunks so that during re-open and re-save scenarios only the differences between client and server are sent over the network.
A feature that allows people to rate list items and documents on a SharePoint site using a 5-star rating system.
The ability to send and receive calls on a desktop phone by using a computer-supported telecommunications application, such as Lync or Communicator.
A feature that provides access to gallery of frequently-used actions with the touch of a button. Users can customize the gallery to execute a combination of operations in one click.
A frame that contains text, shapes, pictures, or other content. A slide is a digital equivalent to a traditional film slide.
A Windows tool used to capture a screen shot, or snip, of any object on the screen, and then annotate, save, or share the image.
To mark an email conversation so that all current and future messages in the conversation are automatically moved to the Deleted Items folder.
A special control that shows pictures, names and titles of people who are attending a meeting, or who are the recipients of an email message.
A console for call handling.
A group of people who can answer calls on behalf of someone else.
A call to a call group that rings the group owner and call group simultaneously. When a member of the group answers the call, the other members get a notification with the status of the call.
A user's work day hours as specified in Microsoft Office Outlook by the day of the week and the start and end times.
To create an indication that the user has an incoming call.
A contact who uses an instant messenger client from AOL, Yahoo!, MSN, or the Windows Live network of Internet services.
An auto-reply text specified using Outlook's Automatic Replies or Out of Office Assistant.
An auto-reply text specified using Outlook's Automatic Replies or Out of Office Assistant.

A feature that merges public switched telephone network (PSTN) and Voice over IP (VoIP) conferences, which allows participants to dial in to a conference from anywhere as an authenticated user without having to be on the corporate network. Typically, a local number is provided to avoid long-distance fees.
An internally or externally hosted service for users to host multiparty conferences from their computers.
A feature that allows the user to apply custom or default markers to items (e.g. Outlook messages or OneNote content) in order to categorize information for easy retrieval and sorting.
A feature that allows the user to apply custom or default markers to items (e.g. Outlook messages or OneNote content) in order to categorize information for easy retrieval and sorting.
A data structure made up of a group of database records. It can originate from a base table or from a query to the table.

A visual depiction of a weighted list. The cloud contains keywords or tags associated with a text or Web site, and formatting (e.g. color and/or size) is used to indicate the relative importance of each item, or frequency with which it occurs.
A feature in Internet Explorer that helps detect phishing websites and can help protect you from installing malicious software or malware.
The feature that allows the user to fill cells with data that follows a pattern or that is based on data in other cells.
The feature that allows the user to fill cells with data that follows a pattern or that is based on data in other cells.
An Internet Explorer feature where the domain of the site you are visiting is darker and the rest of the URL is lighter.
Browsing or navigating through a page using the arrow keys, PAGE UP, PAGE DOWN, HOME and END keys.
A Windows feature that enables your PC to maintain a persistent VPN connection across network changes.

A protected link between two or more objects. During execution, permissions are not checked across the object relationship once it has been established and credentials don't have to be checked several times. This type of link is useful when it is not appropriate or manageable to give permissions to many dependent objects.

A software object that consists of three software plug-in components: a sensor adapter, engine adapter and storage adapter. These adapters are plug-ins for the Windows Biometric Service and are used to capture and process biometric samples, as well as create, store, and match biometric templates.
A set of data resulting from the measurement of one specific characteristic of a single individual. Examples of a biometric sample would be the image of one fingerprint or one iris scan.
The process of creating and sending text messages between or to mobile phones and devices using the SMS protocol.

Any hardware or software that can detect events or environmental changes, such as your current location or the amount of light around your computer. For example, a notebook with a location sensor, such as a Global Positioning System (GPS) receiver, can determine your exact location. An ambient light sensor can detect when there is a change in lighting, and then a program can use that information to adjust the brightness of your screen.

A device that includes an antenna, a radio receiver, and a processor for use with the worldwide GPS (Global Positioning System). A GPS receiver uses position and time information from four GPS satellites to calculate precise information about its current location, its speed of travel, and the current time.
A category of sensor that can detect the current location of your computer.
A Windows feature that helps users to build better queries by enabling them to click on suggested filters, based on what the user is typing, to add them to a search.

Technologies that measure and analyze physical and behavioral human characteristics, such as fingerprints, eye retinas and irises, voice patterns, facial patterns, hand measurements, typing patterns and signatures, to recognize or authenticate identity.
A container for catalogs of software objects such as class libraries, forms, buttons, etc.
A library of controls that support user interface development. Some of these controls function as containers for other controls or content, such as images and media.

An adapter that performs various core biometric operations: cleanup of sensor data, feature extraction, template generation, matching, and indexing. These functions can either be implemented by software in the engine adapter, or by the engine adapter making use of some piece of processing hardware.

An adapter that acts as a wrapper around the physical sensor, and provides a standard interface for configuring the sensor, capturing samples, and controlling the flow of biometric data from the sensor into the processing engine.
Pertaining to a processor memory architecture that stores numbers so that the least significant byte is placed first.

An adapter that provides an interface for managing biometric template databases. This includes operations such as adding and deleting templates, as well as looking up templates either by user identity or by biometric content.

A system that is used to gather a wide variety of information about applications. It includes, but is not limited to, what shims are applied, what compatibility switching context is used, if PCA applies a layer, and it includes Application Impact Telemetry.

A compression container format (.cr8) in Windows that largely replaces the CAB format in all servicing scenarios. This format extends beyond servicing and is a compression solution for file sharing in general.

A Windows service that is designed to aggregate network information (connection availability/status, profiles lists, radio state/strength, etc.) from infrastructure networks so that it can be presented to the user in a meaningful way. The main function of the UCM service includes making connection decisions (connect/disconnect) based on policy across multiple media types. The UCM service also allows for third-party media types to be seamlessly integrated into the system making the UCM expandable with future media types.
Previous searches that are recommended to users based on what they are typing.
A Windows view that provides easy results organization by date, type, author, tag or folder (Arrange "by Folder", "by Author", etc.).
An area within the Windows Control Panel that provides support for sensors such as enabling, disabling or uninstalling sensors and sensor-enabled applications, changing sensor settings, etc.
A light sensor that tracks light in the surroundings and therefore the amount of backlight needed for the LCD screen to be adjusted accordingly.
A device that contains many sensors (thermometer, rain gauge, barometer, etc.) to measure atmospheric data such as temperature, air pressure or humidity.

A package of market-specific content delivered in Windows for 20 target markets. A Local Pack contains market-customized themes (wallpapers, sound schemes, etc.) and locally flavored Internet Explorer favorites and RSS feeds.

A utility that allows recording step-by-step user actions in Windows and storing them in an MHTML file to help developers reproduce and investigate applications problems easily. It also enables end users to share application problems (e.g. with Technical Support) with comprehensive descriptions.

A feature that automatically configures the default printer based on the user's network location. When a mobile user changes network locations, the default printer also changes to the correct one for that network, as defined by the user.
A Windows extensible tool that is used by both Microsoft and OEMs to have a common depth analysis of the first boot experience and address any issues.
An area within the Windows Control Panel that allows the user to designate his home coordinates or address for location-aware functionalities.
An arrangement of search results ordered by relevance using a special search algorithm.
A mode that enables administrators to configure User Account Control to run in auto-elevation mode (i.e. “auto-approval”) for specific times.

A framework that provides a single point for IT professionals and OEMs to service and maintain Windows images offline through a scriptable command line utility and an easily extensible infrastructure.

A framework that provides a single point for IT professionals and OEMs to service and maintain Windows images offline through a scriptable command line utility and an easily extensible infrastructure.

Capability to use default settings and algorithms of Windows Easy Transfer to capture user files and settings. This capability includes logic to determine additional file types that may have been created or modified by users. Without default logic, capture is based on defined manifest of where to look for and what file formats to look for.

arabic: الإزالة التلقائية للعميل من مجموعة متعددة البث
desc: Ability to automatically remove a client from a multicast group (usually a client with lower bandwidth - to be served via unicast deployment), have it join a different multicast group or to terminate deployment.

arabic: واجهة برمجة التطبيقات لخدمات ويب في Windows
desc: A native-code implementation of SOAP that provides a foundation for building Web services for internal Microsoft customers such as components of Windows and parts of Office.
A feature that helps client machines to provide basic protection against denial-of-service attacks.
The process of reverting to legacy code when Windows detects that an application needs it to run seamlessly for the end user.
A type of user state capture that can be performed within Windows Preinstallation Environment phase without needing to boot into full OS.
A feature that enables users to easily discover and use their cell phone’s data capabilities to connect their laptop to the Internet.
A gadget that users can display on their desktop, rather than on the Windows Sidebar. Examples are clocks, news headlines, slide shows, and weather forecasts.
Automatic display adjustment that changes the brightness of your PC screen (laptop and desktop) using light environment information provided by the ambient light sensor.
An option in Microsoft Virtual Earth that allows the user to view an object in a 45-degree angle from above in bird's eye view.

arabic: تقنيات استكشاف الأخطاء وإصلاحها لـ Windows
desc: The overall set of troubleshooting technologies that includes a troubleshooting platform (Windows Troubleshooting Platform), a set of Web services, a toolkit (Windows Troubleshooting Toolkit), and an SDK to encourage third parties and OEMs to develop troubleshooting capabilities.

arabic: النظام الأساسي لاستكشاف الأخطاء وإصلاحها لـ Windows
desc: The engine that executes the Windows Troubleshooting Packs across the operating system.

arabic: حزمة استكشاف الأخطاء وإصلاحها لـ Windows
desc: A type of pack that is developed for the Windows Solution Center (using the Windows Troubleshooting Pack Designer) to perform data collection and analysis to provide users and IT professionals with only those solutions that apply to their PC at the time of viewing.

The underlying engine below Math Ink Panel and Math Result Panel that enables converting handwritten math expressions into electronic format (MathML) thus facilitating writing math formulas in a natural way.

A radio navigation system developed by the U.S. Department of Defense that uses a constellation of 24 earth satellites, which are monitored by ground-based control stations, to provide precise, continuous worldwide positioning and timing information.

The process of linking Windows user accounts to Windows Live IDs or other online accounts, allowing seamless interaction between the two authentication models. As a result, users can be automatically logged into their online services when logging into Windows. They can also share with other users based on their Windows Live IDs (or other), granting them specific permissions to files and folders (read only, read-write, etc.).
An Access 2007 database (.accdb) file with all modules compiled and all editable source code removed.
An Access 2007 database (.accdb) file with all modules compiled and all editable source code removed.
Part of the Access database system that retrieves and stores data in user and system databases. The engine can be thought of as a data manager on which database systems are built.
The list that appears when you click the arrow in the Action column of the Macro object tab.
The process of gathering information by sending and receiving HTML forms or InfoPath forms from Access.
A set of objects that can include tables, queries, forms, reports, macros, and code modules that are designed to work together to make a database easier to use.
A tool that builds a report that contains detailed information about the objects in a database.
The object tab in which you create and modify a macro.
A database or project file for Microsoft Access.
A client/server data engine that provides local data storage on a smaller computer system and that is compatible with Microsoft SQL Server 2000 and prior.
A client/server data engine that provides local data storage on a smaller computer system and that is compatible with Microsoft SQL Server 2000 and prior.
A lookup field that can store more than one value.
A pane that shows objects that have a dependency on the selected object. Also shows objects on which the selected object has dependencies.
A tab that you use to display or work with a database object, such as a table, query, form, or report.
An object tab in which you view, create, and modify relationships between tables and queries.
The horizontal bar above a form or report section in Design view that displays the type and name of the section.
A single set of sign-in credentials (typically, email address and password) that is used to access the services provided by an online service provider (OSP).
A single set of sign-in credentials (typically, email address and password) that is used to access the services provided by an online service provider (OSP).
A provider of online services like email, messaging, and others (example: Windows Live, Yahoo, Google).
A provider of online services like email, messaging, and others (example: Windows Live, Yahoo, Google).
A type of search that returns richer results such as graphics and images, helping you find exactly what you’re looking for, quickly and easily.
A 2-byte multilingual character code.
The process of maintaining connectivity outside of one's usual service or coverage area.
A connection that enables the transmission of data.

A handler that displays a lightweight, read-only preview of a file’s contents without launching the application associated with the file. For example, a preview handler displays a Shell item in the Windows Explorer preview pane.
A call that originates from your mobile device.

A type of attenuation (commonly used in radio music) where a reduction in the volume of an audio stream is triggered by some external event, e.g. when you are using your PC to place or receive phone calls.
A menu item that enables the user to add a word marked as a misspelling to the dictionary used by the spelling checker.
An email that a customer does not want delivered to their inbox, including spam and phishing messages (identified by the mail service) and messages from blocked senders and domains.
An email that a customer does not want delivered to their inbox, including spam and phishing messages (identified by the mail service) and messages from blocked senders and domains.

arabic: عامل تصفية البريد الإلكتروني غير الهام
desc: An email filter that enables the user to set the strictness level that keeps junk email from being delivered to their Inbox.
The default version that includes drag-and-drop functionality, right-click menus, and a reading pane.
The version that uses checkboxes and does not include a reading pane. It is recommneded for users with a slow internet connection.
The part of a sales order that specifies the detailed information about a requested item.
A Web content and metadata syndication format based on XML that describes feeds.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to show nonsequential information.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to show steps in a process or timeline.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to show a continual process.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to show a hierarchical structure, such as an organization chart, or a decision tree.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to illustrate connections.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to show how parts relate to a whole.
A SmartArt graphic layout type that includes layouts designed to show proportional relationships with the largest component on the top or bottom.

A post, comments, and responses made within a conversation space, such as a message board, help board, community, newsgroup, or blog. These exchanges are usually publicly viewable. Participation may require credentials, such as a Windows Live ID.

The descriptive information about a user that is shown to other users. This editable information is separate from the registration information they provide to establish their Windows Live account. This separation allows users to disclose or conceal personal information as they choose.
An answer that only the user knows for a specific question. The answer is used to confirm someone's identity if they forget their password.

A security type that helps prevent unauthorized persons from discerning that a user is going to the Windows Live sign-in page. Otherwise, an unauthorized person might be able to intercept and manipulate the code on the sign-in page, which could result in user information being transmitted to an unauthorized website.
A function that allows a user to call a computer.

arabic: دور التحكم في الوصول استناداً إلى الدور
desc: The user role that is assigned to a user account, which determines the options that are visible to that user and the tasks that the user can perform in the management interface for Exchange Labs.
An act in which a person or program successfully identifies as another by falsifying data, such as email sender, IP connection, or biometrics to gain an illegitimate advantage.
A service that enables customers to implement Windows Live communication services within their own personal domains.

A character code with a null value; literally, a character meaning "nothing." Although it is real in the sense of being recognizable, occupying space internally in the computer, and being sent or received as a character, a NUL character displays nothing, takes no space on the screen or on paper, and causes no specific action when sent to a printer. In ASCII, NUL is represented by the character code 0.
A company that is accredited to sell Internet domain names.
A delegate that is handled through curried functions.
A data visualization tool that helps users analyze complex information using a hierarchical scheme.
A metric that is based on the result of an expression, rather than originating from a data source.

A type of countdown timer that is initially set to 30 days during which you must activate an installation of Windows. If you do not activate Windows within the 30 day period and do not reset the activation clock, Windows will enter Reduced Functionality Mode.

A list of files that are not compressed when capturing an image using ImageX. Some files do not shrink in size when compressed. When capturing an image, you can identify these files to ImageX to save time. These files will still be captured, but ImageX will not attempt to compress them.
The process by which a driver file is copied to a location on the destination computer and the corresponding service is created.
A disk image provided for use in repairing or reinstalling an installation of Windows.

A group whose members can manage all domain controllers in a single domain. This group does not exist on workstations, stand-alone servers, or member servers. Administrative tasks that can be performed by members of this group include logging on locally, creating and deleting network shared resources, starting and stopping services, backing up and restoring files, formatting the hard disk of the computer, and shutting down the computer.
A mode which prevents users from logging on to the computer until Windows is activated.
A mode which prevents users from logging on to the computer until Windows is activated.
The person whom, or place that, a caller is calling.
A driver that must be available in order for the operating system to successfully complete the boot process. Boot critical drivers include all boot start drivers.

The process of installing packages and other updates to a Windows image that is not currently running. For example, you can update a Windows image with security updates, language packs, or other packages.

A language pack that is present in the langpacks folder, but is not yet installed to the Windows image. To install an available language, you must run Windows Setup. Optionally, you can use the Lpksetup.exe tool to install a language pack after Windows is installed.
A computer that does not have an operating system installed.
The process of capturing information at the file level into a single volume, with metadata describing the files.
A language in which 100 percent of Windows resources have been translated. Fully localized languages are always included in full language packs.

A language which contains 100 percent of the resources for that language and locale, but not all of the resources are translated in the language pack. Partially localized languages are installed on top of a fully localized language pack. For example, Arabic (Saudi Arabia) is a partially localized language pack and contains 80 percent of the language resources localized in Arabic. The remaining 20 percent of the language resources can be in either English or French. Both English and French are fully localized languages.
When creating a Windows image, the process of capturing every non-blank sector into a physical file. This is not the process used by ImageX.

The collection of files released with Windows. This collection includes the langpacks directory, the sources directory, and other directories and files required for Windows Setup. In some scenarios, language packs must be copied to the langpacks directory and not installed directly into the .wim file.
A recognition feature that helps increase input speed and reduce effort by providing users with word completion and next word prediction alternates as the user is writing/typing.
A multi-touch gesture that consists of two fingers tapping at the same time and with a relative short distance between each other.
An extension of the conventional touch input feature to allow multiple fingers touching the computer or device screen at the same time.
An extension of the conventional touch input feature to allow multiple fingers touching the computer or device screen at the same time.
A multi-touch gesture that consists of one or two fingers moving in the same direction, parallel to each other.
A multi-touch gesture that consists of one or two fingers moving in the same direction, parallel to each other.
A multi-touch gesture that consists of two fingers moving in opposite directions (-> <- or <- ->).
A multi-touch gesture that consists of either a left-down movement, or right-down, right-up or left-down, right-down, left-up, right-up (roll).
A multi-touch gesture that consists of two fingers moving around a center point or one finger moving around a finger that is not moving.
The engine that specifically recognizes and processes touch input and multi-touch input as commands.
The worldwide collection of networks and gateways that use the TCP/IP suite of protocols to communicate with one another.
The worldwide collection of networks and gateways that use the TCP/IP suite of protocols to communicate with one another.
The worldwide collection of networks and gateways that use the TCP/IP suite of protocols to communicate with one another.
An instance of a channel endpoint participating in the mesh that implements the Peer Channel Protocol.

A workspace offered by a publisher, consisting of applications, shared desktops, and personal desktops (at least some of which are accessed remotely). Each user gets a personally filtered view of the items in the remote workspace.

A computing resource or application that is offered in a remote workspace. Remote Desktop Server provides applications and desktops as remote resources. Other types of remote resources can be defined through extensibility.
A full desktop environment that is personalized for and “owned” by an individual user, as opposed to a shared desktop which does not carry much user personalization.
A Windows tool that users may use to report their issues to Microsoft.
Silent and unexpected process termination by the process itself or by another application.
To shut down a core processor for power saving purpose.
To reopen a core processor that had been parked for power saving purpose.

arabic: النسخ على القرص المضغوط بلا فراغات
desc: A feature of Windows Media Player that allows users to remove gaps between tracks that they burn to audio CDs.

arabic: النسخ على القرص المضغوط بلا فراغات
desc: A feature of Windows Media Player that allows users to remove gaps between tracks that they burn to audio CDs.
Existing in reference to the removal of silences or clicks between tracks when they are burnt to an audio CD or when they are played back from the CD.
A behind-the-scene service that is part of Credential Manager and that actually does the work of creating and managing user credentials to allow users to log on across machines and sites.
A triplet that identifies a color from its red, green and blue components.
A unique identifier made from four otherwise separate pieces of information. For example, a color can be specified by a black, yellow, magenta and cyan quad.
A quad that identifies a color from its black, yellow, magenta and cyan components.
A color model that describes color information in terms of the black (K), yellow (Y), Magenta (M) and Cyan (C) intensities that make up the color.

The primary interface used to enable sharing media to other computers and devices, and to access media sharing settings and devices that interact with the media sharing feature. If you enable sharing you can play your favorite music, videos, and pictures on any computer or device in any room in your home.

The primary interface used to enable sharing media to other computers and devices, and to access media sharing settings and devices that interact with the media sharing feature. If you enable sharing you can play your favorite music, videos, and pictures on any computer or device in any room in your home.

arabic: إدارة بيانات اعتماد المقاييس الحيوية لـ Windows
desc: The Windows component that stores and manages biometric credentials such as fingerprints.

arabic: موفر بيانات اعتماد بصمات الأصابع لـ Windows
desc: The Windows component that provides fingerprint information that is used to gain access to local and network resources.
Any information (e.g. account numbers, sensitive data, etc.) with a title and some free-form text that can be stored in a secure manner in a personal vault.
To make an object, such as a file, accessible.
The page for creating and administering individual user accounts, and adding new administrators.
The area of the Organizations page where hosted customers can set up additional domains.
The main Administration Center page, from which all other monitoring and managing functions are accessible via columns, tabs, and pop-up windows.
The option on the Spam Filter page for turning off spam and virus filtering at the individual user level.

english: Allow Users to Log in to Spam Quarantine option
arabic: السماح للمستخدم بتسجيل الدخول إلى خيار عزل البريد العشوائي
desc: The option on the Spam Quarantine page that controls access to the Spam Quarantine Web site for a specific user.
An extended HTML element that is used to describe the class of a viewable or downloadable document. It can be misused to pass dangerous attachments; EHS allows users to block this tag.
Entries in the Administration Center for main personnel, technical personnel, and billing personnel within the specified organization.

An area on the Spam Filter page that gives IT administrators the ability to select various content attributes of a message that either increase the potential for the message to be quarantined as spam (the "spam score") or absolutely quarantine messages that contain specific attributes.
A feature of the Hosted Filtering service that verifies intended recipients against an approved user list before email is processed for spam, viruses, and other malicious software.
The options on the Directory Services page for how mail to users in the Directory Services user lists is handled: Pass Through, Reject Test, Reject, Group Filtering, and Intelligent Routing.
The method of adding new users to an organization's service. There are three upload modes: Administration Center mode, Directory Synchronization Tool mode, and Secure FTP mode.
The page where customer administrators activate and customize filtering services at the domain level.

An option reached from the Rule Management area of the Policy Filter page for outbound mail. With this rule, email messages that are sent by users in the organization can be encrypted automatically based on rule matching by subject and message keywords, regular expressions, sending and receiving email address, and domains.

Hosted spam and virus filtering from an Exchange Hosted Services provider. Users’ email is filtered according to rules managed by the organization's administrators. Users and administrators are given varying rights to adjust the filtering rules.
An option on the Policy Filter page for setting an expiration date. This option can be specified for any policy rule.
The capability for users to enter a specific email address to receive a copy of every message submitted as a "false positive," a message that is identified as spam when it is not.

The company that originally owned the Microsoft spam and virus filtering service that is now part of Exchange Hosted Services. The word "FrontBridge" still appears in URLs, email addresses, and elsewhere.
A feature of Directory Services that provides the ability for different groups of users to have their own sets of filtering rules, even if all users share the same domain.

An HTML email reminder that gives users a snapshot of the new spam messages delivered to their Spam Quarantine mailbox since their last notification, or since the last time they logged in to Spam Quarantine, whichever is most recent. From this reminder email, users can scan the list of messages that have been filtered and salvage messages or report them as false positives directly from the notification.
The IP address that inbound email is delivered to after it has been processed by the Hosted Filtering service. Inbound Mail Server addresses are defined for each domain in your organization.
A feature of Group Filtering that routes SMTP addresses to specific delivery locations based on group names and associations, even if all users share the same domain.

arabic: خيار تقييد الوصول إلى عزل البريد العشوائي عبر عنوان IP
desc: The option on the Spam Filter page that restricts access to monitoring and managing Spam Quarantine by IP address.
An option on the Policy Filter page that blocks messages that use special header information to split emails into several messages, which could be used to send viruses.
The option on the Policy Filter page for delivering spam email messages to the recipient with an identifying word or phrase in the subject line.
The page where administrators set up notifications for a situation in which their email is being deferred by the filtering service.
The page that contains general information, virus updates, and network alerts.
The option on the Spam Filter page for selecting a language other than English for Spam Quarantine notifications.

english: Notify when new spam is received option
arabic: خيار الإعلام عند تلقي بريد عشوائي جديد
desc: The check box that has users receive periodic email reminders to review their newly filtered spam mail.
The page in the Administration Center that details all hosted organizations in a customer's account.

The area on the Organizations page that displays outbound addresses when the service is configured and set up. Hosted customers need to request EHS Technical Support to add or remove addresses that are currently subject to outbound EHS filtering.
A list on the Organizations page that displays all outbound IP addresses that have been configured to use the outbound scanning services in the Hosted Filtering network.
